title: Stage 0 — shared definitions
description: Definitions every Stage 0 record type draws on. Shape only: these say what a field looks like, never which value is correct. A schema that could reject a legally-correct answer has encoded a judgement and is out of scope for this repo to write (CLAUDE.md rule 1).

upstream_ref.description: An upstream ref, stored verbatim — `TMM/Part22/1/1/2`, `TMA1995/s43`, `TMA1995/s41(3)(a)`. Never an IRI (docs/IDENTIFIERS.md §4). The pattern here is a coarse gate; the authority is `tm_knowledge.refs.parse_ref`, which the validator applies to every field carrying `format: upstream-ref`.

span.description: Character offsets into the upstream `text`, `[start, end]`. Null while the record is being transcribed and the offsets have not been resolved — a gap to report, not a value to invent (P8).

content_hash.description: The `content_hash` the source passage carried when this record was made. When it stops matching the pinned snapshot the record is stale and returns to review (docs/IDENTIFIERS.md §5).

approved_by.description: The expert who approved this record. Null is permitted by the *schema* and rejected by the completeness gate: a record without it is not approved knowledge (CLAUDE.md rule 4). The schema's job is to make the gap visible, not to make an unapproved record unwritable — an agent must be able to transcribe an expert's words into a well-formed record that is then reported as awaiting approval (P8, P10).

notes.description: Free text. Never parsed, never validated for content.

tier.description: 1 deterministic · 2 low-risk · 3 legally significant (ADR-0008). Which tier a statement belongs in is an expert's call; the schema only knows there are three.
